description: We are Artemis IV, a team of six from Ceara/Brazil, named after the mission planned to return astronauts to the Moon’s surface.
summary:
Mars Outpost Junior Astronaut Trainer is a free, web-based educational strategy game for children aged 7–12, requiring no login or download. Over a 10-to-14-sol (Martian day) mission, players command a base and navigate real-world engineering trade-offs, balancing limited energy, life support, food production, radiation shielding, and scientific research.

Rather than oversimplifying space exploration or overwhelming kids with complex simulators, the game turns authentic NASA data from DONKI, the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), and Mars missions into tangible daily challenges where every choice has a cost. Each event cites its NASA source and ends with a “Commander’s Report” explaining the science behind the outcome.

Kids can play solo or as a crew, debating alerts, forming predictions before each sol, and learning constructively from the consequences of their collective decisions. By replacing passive quizzes with active resource management, Mars Outpost empowers children, families, and educators to think like real mission planners, advancing inclusive science education in alignment with SDG 4.
details:
Mars Outpost – Junior Astronaut Trainer is an educational web strategy game where children aged 7–12 command a Mars base over a 10- to 14-sol mission.

Each day follows a 5-step loop:

  1. Daily Briefing: Real environmental or space weather events.
  2. Control Panel: Simple gauges for Energy, Life Support, Food, Radiation Shield, Science, and Crew Morale.
  3. Choice with a Cost: Following the golden rule "no choice is free," every decision forces an immediate engineering trade-off.
  4. Immediate Consequence: Direct visual feedback.
  5. Commander’s Report: A constructive end-of-mission scientific diagnosis instead of frustrating penalties.

In multiplayer mode, kids act as a crew, debating and negotiating decisions together. Rather than relying on passive quizzes or overwhelming simulators, scenarios use curated NASA data from DONKI, OSDR, and Mars/Artemis missions, complete with transparency badges.

Free, browser-based, and requiring no login or downloads, Mars Outpost features a Portuguese interface and Family/Classroom discussion cards. Aligned with SDG 4, it democratizes space engineering for Lusophone audiences, developing systems thinking and scientific literacy.

Tech Stack: HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, NASA DONKI & OSDR, Blender, Codex, Claude, Git/GitHub, Vercel, and Oracle.
